title: New desk on the wrong VLAN
symptom: A newly set-up desk gets an IP from a different network and cannot reach shared drives
user_description: I moved to the new desk by the window. Internet sort of works but I can't open any shared drives or the printer. The PC next to me works fine.

options.why: The PC connects fine. It is simply on the wrong network for that port.

options.text: Swap his PC for another one
options.why: Any PC on that wall port would get the same wrong network.

options.text: Give the PC a static IP from the office range by hand
options.why: It would still be on the wrong VLAN, and a hand-set address can clash with others.

options.text: Compare its IP address with a neighbour's. A different range suggests the wall port is on the wrong VLAN, so escalate to the network team
options.why: Each VLAN hands out its own address range. A different range on one desk points to how that port is set on the switch.

hints: What is different between his PC and the working one next to him?
What does a different IP range suggest?
Who can change how a switch port is set up?
real_world_tip: Run ipconfig on both PCs. Seeing a different range, like a guest or phone network, is the quickest clue.

escalation.team_why: VLANs are set on the switch ports, which the network team manages.

details.text: The desk and wall port number
details.why: Tells them which switch port to change.

details.text: The IP address it gets, and a neighbour's for comparison
details.why: Shows clearly that it is on a different network.

details.text: What does not work (shared drives and printer)
details.why: Confirms the effect of being on the wrong VLAN.

details.text: Set a static IP from the office range on the PC
details.why: Hides the problem instead of fixing the port, and can cause address conflicts.
